comment: The distinction between foundational identity and health-sector identification is highly relevant. The guidance should state more explicitly that assignment of a health identifier and access to essential care must not depend on possession of a civil or national identity document.

anchor.note: p.13 l.195–207; Box 1.2 read as the printed page; section 1.2.1 agrees

public.text: The distinction between foundational identity and health-sector identification is highly relevant. The guidance should state more explicitly that assignment of a health identifier and access to essential care must not depend on possession of a civil or national identity document.
public.suggestedRevision: Add: “A person shall be able to receive a health identifier and access essential health services without possessing a civil or national identity document. The Client Registry should support temporary identifiers, probabilistic matching, deduplication and subsequent linkage to civil identity when available.”
